entities.summary: Sayyid Moḥammad Abdallah Hassan was a Somali scholar, poet, military leader and religious, cultural and political figure who founded and headed the Somali Dervish movement, which led a holy war against British, Italian and Ethiopian colonial intrusions in the Somali Peninsula. He was pejoratively known by the British Empire as the "Mad Mullah." In 1917, the Ottoman Empire referred to him as the "Emir of the Somali People." Due to his successful completion of the Hajj to Mecca, his assertion of being the descendant of the Islamic prophet Muhammad and his complete memorization of the Quran, his name is preluded with honorifics such as Hajji, Hafiz, Emir, Sheikh, Mullah or Sayyid.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Muhammad ʿAbdallah Hasan's leadership of the Somali Dervish movement led to a holy war against colonial intrusions in the Somali Peninsula, resulting in significant regional instability and ultimately contributing to the collapse of the Ottoman Empire's influence in East Africa. His assertion of being the descendant of Muhammad and his complete memorization of the Quran earned him honorifics such as Hajji and Emir.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a military leader and religious figure, Sayyid Moḥammad Abdallah Hassan's Somali Dervish movement resisted colonial intrusions in the Somali Peninsula, leading to the Scramble for Africa. His assertion of being the descendant of Muhammad and his completion of the Hajj cemented his influence on East African politics.
